tutorial.title: How igrasp-demo starts: a tour of igrasp-demo
tutorial.intro: You will follow igrasp-demo from src/main.ts to its Makefile, its architecture page and its decisions.
tutorial.subject: How igrasp-demo starts

chapters.title: The entry point: main() in src/main.ts
chapters.goal: Explain how src/main.ts builds the greeting and when it is shouted.
chapters.hootIntro: Hoot starts where igrasp-demo starts: main() in src/main.ts.

steps.title: Where igrasp-demo starts
steps.body: The README points at `src/main.ts` lines 9-12: `main()` takes `Options` and returns the greeting from `greet(name)`.

steps.title: From the import to the call

stops.annotation: src/main.ts imports `greet` from `./greet`: the greeting is not built here.
`Options` has a `name` and an optional `loud` flag.
`main()` defaults `loud` to false and upper-cases the message only when asked.

steps.title: Find the shout
steps.prompt: Click the line of main() that decides whether igrasp-demo shouts.
steps.explanation: Line 11 of src/main.ts returns `message.toUpperCase()` when `loud` is true, the message otherwise.

steps.question: What does main() in src/main.ts return when loud is false?
choices: The message as greet made it
steps.hint: Read the ternary at the end of main() in src/main.ts.
steps.explanation: main() returns `loud ? message.toUpperCase() : message`, so with loud false it is the message from greet(name).

takeaways: main() in src/main.ts gets its message from greet(name).
Options.loud defaults to false in main().
Line 11 of src/main.ts upper-cases the message only when loud.

questions.quote: return loud ? message.toUpperCase() : message; # the shout
questions.question: Why is the shout decided in main() and not in greet()?
questions.answer:
Because `greet()` only builds the message: src/main.ts keeps the `loud` option.

For example:

```ts
main({ name: "Ada", loud: true });
```

returns `HELLO, ADA`.

questions.question: What does "true" mean here: 0123?
questions.answer: Nothing special: it is a string.

chapters.title: Build and test with the Makefile
chapters.goal: Explain the build and test targets of the Makefile and how CI runs make test.
chapters.hootIntro: Hoot runs the Makefile of igrasp-demo, the way its CI does.

steps.title: Two targets in the Makefile
steps.body: The igrasp-demo Makefile has `build` (`npm run build`) and `test` (`npm test`); package.json maps them to `tsc` and `vitest run`.

steps.title: From a push to the tests
steps.prompt: Put what happens after a push to igrasp-demo in order.
items: ci.yml starts the test job on push
steps.explanation: ci.yml triggers on push and runs `make test`; the Makefile calls `npm test`, which package.json maps to `vitest run`.

steps.title: Which file does what
steps.prompt: Match each file of igrasp-demo to its job.

pairs.right: names the build and test targets
maps the npm scripts to tsc and vitest
runs make test on every push

steps.explanation: The Makefile is the entry, package.json holds the scripts, and .github/workflows/ci.yml runs `make test` on push.

steps.title: Run the tests of igrasp-demo
steps.instruction: In a terminal at the root of igrasp-demo, run the Makefile's `test` target and watch vitest run.
steps.expected: npm test runs vitest run, as package.json says.

takeaways: The Makefile has build and test targets.
package.json maps them to tsc and vitest run.
ci.yml runs make test on every push.

questions.question: Can I run it without make?
questions.answer: Yes: `npm test` runs the same `vitest run` (package.json).

chapters.title: The architecture page of igrasp-demo
chapters.goal: Explain the flowchart of docs/architecture.md: who owns the folder and who renders.
chapters.hootIntro: Hoot adjusts his glasses over docs/architecture.md.

steps.title: The two halves
steps.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  UI[React UI] -->|invoke| Rust[Rust backend]
  Rust -->|events| UI
  Rust --> FS[(Folder)]
steps.caption: The flowchart of docs/architecture.md: only the Rust backend touches the folder.

steps.title: Invoke and events
steps.concept: In a desktop app split in two processes, the UI asks the native side with commands and listens to its events.
steps.applied: In igrasp-demo, docs/architecture.md draws `React UI -->|invoke| Rust backend` and `Rust -->|events| UI`: the backend owns the file system.

steps.title: Who owns the folder
steps.body: docs/architecture.md says "The backend owns the file system; the frontend renders" (line 12).

steps.question: In docs/architecture.md, the React UI of igrasp-demo reads the folder itself.
steps.hint: Follow the arrow to the Folder node in docs/architecture.md.
steps.explanation: Only `Rust --> FS[(Folder)]` reaches the folder; the UI invokes the backend.

takeaways: docs/architecture.md splits igrasp-demo in a React UI and a Rust backend.
The UI invokes the backend; the backend sends events.
Only the backend touches the folder.
